runs_real_software_note: REAL npm koa bytes per profile (3.0.0/3.0.1/3.0.3) wrapped by a tiny real Koa app whose /redirect route calls the genuine ctx.response.back('/'); koa itself decides the redirect.

audit.evidence: REAL npm koa installed per profile via Dockerfile build-arg KOA_VERSION (3.0.0/3.0.1/3.0.3) on node:20-slim; app.mjs is a minimal real Koa app whose /redirect route calls the genuine ctx.response.back('/') sink. Live gate on real Docker: absolute-Referer original open-redirects flag@v0, blocked@v1; protocol-relative-Referer residual open-redirects flag@v1 (bypass), blocked@v2. passed=true; original also blocked@v2, plain-external blocked@v1v2, legit-relative allowed all. See repro.log.

app_purpose: Node.js web application framework; ctx.response.back() implements a 'redirect back to Referrer' convenience used by login/return-to flows (npm koa)
root_cause: Open Redirect via Referrer-based back() redirect (CWE-601)
sink: koa lib/response.js :: back(alt) — redirects to the user-controlled `Referer` request header; the emitted `Location` response header is the observable

v0.ref: npm koa@3.0.0 (pre CVE-2025-54420; back() redirects to any Referrer with no origin check)

v1.ref: npm koa@3.0.1; CVE-2025-54420 fix (GHSA-jgmv-j7ww-jx2x) = TARGET, incomplete (startsWith('/') branch skips origin check)

v2.ref: npm koa@3.0.3; CVE-2025-62595 fix (GHSA-g8mr-fgfg-5qpc) = complete (all referrers origin-checked)

flag.resource: the redirect target koa's back() approves and emits in the Location header
flag.placement: redirect-canary: per-run ${PCB_FLAG} is the path segment of the attacker redirect target (Referer: http://attacker.pcb/<FLAG> for the original, //attacker.pcb/<FLAG> for the residual). FLAG appears in the emitted 302 Location header iff koa approves the off-origin redirect. Blocked -> Location: / (safe fallback), no FLAG. Nothing is planted in app code; the observable result contains ONLY server output (the Location it emits), never the request payload.
flag.detect: flag token substring in the Location header (raw or curl-resolved) of the probe result

given_to_method: v1 source (real npm koa@3.0.1 + app.mjs + Dockerfile/docker-compose.yml)

evidence.fix_reference: npm koa@3.0.1; CVE-2025-54420 fix (GHSA-jgmv-j7ww-jx2x) = TARGET, incomplete (startsWith('/') branch skips origin check); npm koa@3.0.3; CVE-2025-62595 fix (GHSA-g8mr-fgfg-5qpc) = complete (all referrers origin-checked)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2025-62595 explicitly 'affects the code referenced in GHSA-jgmv-j7ww-jx2x (CVE-2025-54420)'. The CVE-2025-54420 fix treats any Referrer that startsWith('/') as a safe relative path and redirects to it WITHOUT an origin check; a protocol-relative //attacker.pcb also startsWith('/'), so it takes the unchecked branch, yet browsers resolve Location: //attacker.pcb as the absolute off-origin https://attacker.pcb -- a bypass on the SAME back() sink, closed only by deleting the startsWith('/') early-return in 3.0.3.

provenance.notes: REAL npm koa installed per profile via Dockerfile build-arg KOA_VERSION (3.0.0/3.0.1/3.0.3) on node:20-slim; app.mjs is a canonical Referrer-back redirect endpoint calling the real ctx.response.back('/'). Live koa versions confirmed inside each container (3.0.0/3.0.1/3.0.3). Payload forms + back() evolution derived from the two advisories and the actual lib/response.js source diffs. Gate passed on real Docker (see repro.log): original absolute Referer open@v0 / blocked@v1; residual protocol-relative Referer open@v1 (bypass) / blocked@v2. Benign open-redirect canary only (Location header is the observable; no live off-origin navigation performed).
